title: Arakhin 11
description: The magreifa’s hundred or thousand tones, why the mishna’s musicians were slaves, Israelites or Levites, a dozen verses for the Levites’ song, singers and gatekeepers who trade places, and whether a communal voluntary burnt offering is sung over.
topics: 🎵 The magreifa: ten holes, a hundred tones or a thousand, and the baraita’s exaggeration
🎻 Slaves, Israelites or Levites: song in the mouth, and whether the platform proves lineage and tithes
⚖️ Rabbi Meir and the Rabbis: is the song indispensable to the offering, and why it must be by day
📜 Where the Torah requires the Levites’ song: a dozen verses, from “serve with the name” to “they shall bear”
🍇 First fruits and song: “goodness” and “goodness,” and song only over wine
🚪 Singers who close the gates: Rabbi Yehoshua bar Ḥananya and Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Gudgeda

a1.he: עֲשָׂרָה נְקָבִים הָיוּ בָּהּ, כׇּל אֶחָד וְאֶחָד מוֹצִיא עֲשָׂרָה מִינֵי זֶמֶר, נִמְצֵאת כּוּלָּהּ מוֹצִיאָה מֵאָה מִינֵי זֶמֶר. בְּמַתְנִיתָא תָּנָא: הִיא אַמָּה וּגְבוֹהָ אַמָּה, וְקַתָּא יוֹצָא הֵימֶנָּה, וַעֲשָׂרָה נְקָבִים הָיוּ בָּהּ, כׇּל אֶחָד מוֹצִיא מֵאָה מִינֵי זֶמֶר, נִמְצֵאת כּוּלָּהּ מוֹצִיאָה אֶלֶף מִינֵי זֶמֶר. אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק: וְסִימָנָיךְ מַתְנִיתָא גּוּזְמָא.

a2.he: וְעַבְדֵי כֹהֲנִים הָיוּ כּוּ׳. לֵימָא בְּהָא קָמִיפַּלְגִי, דְּמַאן דְּאָמַר עֲבָדִים הָיוּ קָסָבַר: עִיקַּר שִׁירָה בַּפֶּה, וּכְלִי לְבַסּוֹמֵי קָלָא הוּא דַּעֲבִידָא, וּמַאן דְּאָמַר לְוִיִּם הָיוּ קָסָבַר: עִיקַּר שִׁירָה בִּכְלִי!

a3.he: וְתִסְבְּרָא? רַבִּי יוֹסֵי מַאי קָסָבַר? אִי קָסָבַר: עִיקַּר שִׁירָה בַּפֶּה — עֲבָדִים סַגִּיא, אִי קָסָבַר: עִיקַּר שִׁירָה בִּכְלִי — לְוִיִּם בָּעֵינַן!

a4.he: לְעוֹלָם קָסָבַר: עִיקַּר שִׁירָה בַּפֶּה, וְהָכָא בְּמַעֲלִין מִדּוּכָן לְיוּחֲסִין וּלְמַעַשְׂרוֹת קָמִיפַּלְגִי.

a5.he: מַאן דְּאָמַר עֲבָדִים הָיוּ, קָסָבַר: אֵין מַעֲלִין מִדּוּכָן לֹא לְיוּחֲסִין וְלֹא לְמַעַשְׂרוֹת. מַאן דְּאָמַר לְוִיִּם הָיוּ, קָסָבַר: מַעֲלִין מִדּוּכָן בֵּין לְיוּחֲסִין בֵּין לְמַעַשְׂרוֹת. וּלְמַאן דְּאָמַר יִשְׂרְאֵלִים הָיוּ, קָסָבַר: מַעֲלִין מִדּוּכָן לְיוּחֲסִין וְלֹא לְמַעַשְׂרוֹת.

a6.he: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: הַשִּׁיר מְעַכֵּב אֶת הַקׇּרְבָּן, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי מֵאִיר; וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים: אֵינוֹ מְעַכֵּב.

a7.he: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר? דְּאָמַר קְרָא: ״וָאֶתְּנָה אֶת הַלְוִיִּם נְתֻנִים לְאַהֲרֹן וּלְבָנָיו מִתּוֹךְ בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל... וּלְכַפֵּר עַל בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל״, מָה כַּפָּרָה מְעַכֶּבֶת, אַף שִׁירָה מְעַכֶּבֶת.

a8.he: וְרַבָּנַן? הָהוּא לְאִידַּךְ דְּרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר, דְּאָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: מָה כַּפָּרָה בַּיּוֹם, אַף שִׁירָה בַּיּוֹם.

a9.he: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: מִנַּיִן לְעִיקַּר שִׁירָה מִן הַתּוֹרָה? שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״וְשֵׁרֵת בְּשֵׁם ה׳ אֱלֹהָיו״, אֵיזֶהוּ שֵׁירוּת שֶׁבְּשֵׁם? הֱוֵי אוֹמֵר: זֹה שִׁירָה.

a10.he: וְאֵימָא נְשִׂיאוּת כַּפַּיִם! מִדִּכְתִיב: ״לְשָׁרְתוֹ וּלְבָרֵךְ בִּשְׁמוֹ״, מִכְּלָל דְּבִרְכַּת כֹּהֲנִים לָאו שֵׁירוּת הִיא.

a11.he: רַב מַתְנָה אָמַר מֵהָכָא: ״תַּחַת אֲשֶׁר לֹא עָבַדְתָּ אֶת ה׳ אֱלֹהֶיךָ בְּשִׂמְחָה וּבְטוּב לֵבָב״, אֵיזוֹ הִיא עֲבוֹדָה שֶׁבְּשִׂמְחָה וּבְטוּב לֵבָב? הֱוֵי אוֹמֵר: זֹה שִׁירָה. וְאֵימָא דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה, דִּכְתִיב: ״פִּקּוּדֵי ה׳ יְשָׁרִים מְשַׂמְּחֵי לֵב״! ״מְשַׂמְּחֵי לֵב״ אִיקְּרִי, ״טוֹב״ לָא אִיקְּרִי.

a12.he: וְאֵימָא בִּכּוּרִים, דִּכְתִיב: ״וְשָׂמַחְתָּ בְכׇל הַטּוֹב״! ״טוֹב״ אִיקְּרִי, ״טוּב לֵבָב״ לָא אִיקְּרִי.

a13.he: אָמַר רַב מַתְנָה: מִנַּיִן לַבִּיכּוּרִים שֶׁטְּעוּנִין שִׁירָה? אָתְיָא ״טוֹב״ ״טוֹב״ מֵהָכָא.

a14.he: אִינִי? וְהָא אָמַר רַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר נַחְמָנִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹנָתָן: מִנַּיִן שֶׁאֵין אוֹמְרִים שִׁירָה אֶלָּא עַל הַיַּיִן? שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״וַתֹּאמֶר לָהֶם הַגֶּפֶן הֶחֳדַלְתִּי אֶת תִּירוֹשִׁי הַמְשַׂמֵּחַ אֱלֹהִים וַאֲנָשִׁים״, אִם אֲנָשִׁים מְשַׂמֵּחַ, אֱלֹהִים בַּמֶּה מְשַׂמֵּחַ? מִכָּאן שֶׁאֵין אוֹמְרִים שִׁירָה אֶלָּא עַל הַיַּיִן.

a15.he: מַשְׁכַּחַתְּ לַהּ, כִּדְתָנֵי רַבִּי יוֹסֵי: ״פְּרִי אַתָּה מֵבִיא, וְאִי אַתָּה מֵבִיא מַשְׁקִין״; הֵבִיא עֲנָבִים וּדְרָכָן, מִנַּיִן? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״תָּבִיא״.

a16.he: חִזְקִיָּה אָמַר מֵהָכָא: ״וּכְנַנְיָהוּ שַׂר הַלְוִיִּם יָשׂוֹר בַּמַּשָּׂא כִּי מֵבִין הוּא״, אַל תִּיקְרֵי ״יָשׂוֹר״ אֶלָּא ״יָשִׁיר״.

a17.he: בִּלְוָוטֵי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן, מֵהָכָא: ״לַעֲבוֹד עֲבוֹדַת עֲבוֹדָה״, אֵיזֶהוּ עֲבוֹדָה שֶׁצְּרִיכָה עֲבוֹדָה? הֱוֵי אוֹמֵר: זוֹ שִׁירָה.

a18.he: רַבִּי יִצְחָק אָמַר מֵהָכָא: ״שְׂאוּ זִמְרָה וּתְנוּ תֹף כִּנּוֹר נָעִים עִם נָבֶל״. רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק אָמַר מֵהָכָא: ״הֵם יִשְׂאוּ קוֹלָם יָרֹנּוּ בִּגְאוֹן ה׳ צָהֲלוּ מִיָּם״.

a19.he: וְתַנָּא מַיְיתֵי לַהּ מֵהָכָא: ״וְלִבְנֵי קְהָת לֹא נָתָן כִּי עֲבוֹדַת הַקֹּדֶשׁ עֲלֵיהֶם בַּכָּתֵף יִשָּׂאוּ״, מִמַּשְׁמָע שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר ״בַּכָּתֵף״ אֵינִי יוֹדֵעַ שֶׁ״יִּשְׂאוּ״? מָה תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר ״יִשָּׂאוּ״? אֵין ״יִשָּׂאוּ״ אֶלָּא לְשׁוֹן שִׁירָה, וְכֵן הוּא אוֹמֵר: ״שְׂאוּ זִמְרָה וּתְנוּ תֹף״, וְאוֹמֵר: ״יִשְּׂאוּ קוֹלָם יָרוֹנּוּ וְגוֹ׳״.

a20.he: חֲנַנְיָא בֶּן אֲחִי רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ אָמַר, מֵהָכָא: ״מֹשֶׁה יְדַבֵּר וְהָאֱלֹהִים יַעֲנֶנּוּ בְקוֹל״,

b1.he: עַל עִסְקֵי קוֹל. רַב אָשֵׁי אָמַר, מֵהָכָא: ״וַיְהִי כְאֶחָד לַמְחַצְּצרִים וְלַמְשֹׁרְרִים לְהַשְׁמִיעַ קוֹל אֶחָד״.

b2.he: רַבִּי יוֹנָתָן אָמַר מֵהָכָא: ״וְלֹא יָמוּתוּ גַם הֵם גַּם אַתֶּם״ — מָה אַתֶּם בַּעֲבוֹדַת מִזְבֵּחַ, אַף הֵם בַּעֲבוֹדַת מִזְבֵּחַ.

b3.he: תַּנְיָא נָמֵי הָכִי: ״וְלֹא יָמוּתוּ גַם הֵם גַּם אַתֶּם״ — אַתֶּם בְּשֶׁלָּהֶם וְהֵם בְּשֶׁלָּכֶם בְּמִיתָה, הֵם בְּשֶׁלָּהֶם אֵינָן בְּמִיתָה אֶלָּא בְּאַזְהָרָה.

b4.he: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: נְקִיטִינַן, מְשׁוֹרֵר שֶׁשִּׁיעֵר בְּשֶׁל חֲבֵירוֹ בְּמִיתָה, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״וְהַחֹנִים לִפְנֵי הַמִּשְׁכָּן קֵדְמָה לִפְנֵי אֹהֶל מוֹעֵד וְגוֹ׳ וְהַזָּר הַקָּרֵב יוּמָת״. מַאי זָר? אִילֵּימָא זָר מַמָּשׁ — הָכְתִיב חֲדָא זִימְנָא! אֶלָּא לָאו זָר דְּאוֹתָהּ עֲבוֹדָה.

b5.he: מֵיתִיבִי: מְשׁוֹרֵר שֶׁשִּׁיעֵר וּמְשׁוֹעֵר שֶׁשּׁוֹרֵר, אֵינָן בְּמִיתָה אֶלָּא בְּאַזְהָרָה!

b6.he: תַּנָּאֵי הִיא, דְּתַנְיָא: מַעֲשֶׂה בְּרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בַּר חֲנַנְיָה שֶׁהָלַךְ לְסַיֵּיעַ בְּהַגָּפַת דְּלָתוֹת אֵצֶל רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן גּוּדְגְּדָא, אָמַר לוֹ: בְּנִי, חֲזוֹר לַאֲחוֹרֶיךָ, שֶׁאַתָּה מִן הַמְשׁוֹרְרִים וְלֹא מִן הַמְשׁוֹעֲרִים.

b7.he: מַאי לָאו בְּהָא קָמִיפַּלְגִי, דְּמָר סָבַר: מִיתָה הִיא, וּגְזַרוּ בַּהּ רַבָּנַן, וּמָר סָבַר: אַזְהָרָה הִיא, וְלָא גְּזַרוּ בַּהּ?

b8.he: דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא אַזְהָרָה הִיא, מָר סָבַר: מְסַיֵּיעַ גְּזַרוּ בֵּיהּ רַבָּנַן, וּמָר סָבַר: לָא גְּזַרוּ בֵּיהּ רַבָּנַן.

b9.he: בָּעֵי רַבִּי אָבִין: עוֹלַת נִדְבַת צִיבּוּר טְעוּנָה שִׁירָה אוֹ אֵינָהּ טְעוּנָה שִׁירָה? ״עֹלֹתֵיכֶם״ אָמַר רַחֲמָנָא, אַחַת עוֹלַת חוֹבָה וְאַחַת עוֹלַת נְדָבָה, אוֹ דִלְמָא ״עוֹלוֹתֵיכֶם״ דְּכוּלְּהוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל קָאָמַר רַחֲמָנָא?

b10.he: תָּא שְׁמַע, וַיֹּאמֶר: ״חִזְקִיָּהוּ לְהַעֲלוֹת הָעוֹלָה עַל הַמִּזְבֵּחַ, וּבְעֵת הֵחֵל הָעוֹלָה הֵחֵל שִׁיר ה׳ וְהַחֲצוֹצְרוֹת עַל יְדֵי כְּלֵי שִׁיר דָּוִד מֶלֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵל״. הַאי שִׁירָה מַאי עֲבִידְתַּהּ? אִילֵּימָא דְּעוֹלַת חוֹבָה, לְמָה לֵיהּ אִימְּלוֹכֵי? אֶלָּא לָאו דְּעוֹלַת נְדָבָה.

b11.he: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: לֹא, עוֹלַת רֹאשׁ חוֹדֶשׁ הֲוָה, וְקָא מִיבַּעְיָא לְהוּ מִי הוּקְבַּע רֹאשׁ חֹדֶשׁ בִּזְמַנּוֹ דְּלִיקְרַב אוֹ לָא.

b12.he: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי: וּמִי מָצֵית אָמְרַתְּ הָכִי? וְהָכְתִיב ״בַּיּוֹם שִׁשָּׁה עָשָׂר לַחֹדֶשׁ הָרִאשׁוֹן וְגוֹ׳״, ״וַיֹּאמֶר חִזְקִיָּהוּ לְהַעֲלוֹת הָעוֹלָה עַל הַמִּזְבֵּחַ״!

b13.he: אֶלָּא אָמַר רָמֵי בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יֵיבָא: כֶּבֶשׂ הַבָּא עִם הָעוֹמֶר קָמִיבַּעְיָא לְהוּ, מִי קָבַע רֹאשׁ חֹדֶשׁ בִּזְמַנּוֹ דְּלִיקְרַיב אוֹ לָא?

b14.he: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב אַוְיָא: וְלִיחְזֵי פֶּסַח הֵיכִי עָבֵיד, מַצָּה הֵיכִי אָכֵיל!

b15.he: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: מִידֵּי דְּהָוֵה אַשְּׁלִיחָא דְצִיבּוּרָא דְּמִמְּלִיךְ. הַשְׁתָּא דְּאָתֵית לְהָכִי, אֲפִילּוּ תֵּימָא עוֹלַת חוֹבָה, מִידֵּי דְּהָוֵה אַשְּׁלִיחָא דְצִיבּוּרָא דְּמִמְּלִיךְ.

b16.he: תָּא שְׁמַע: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר: מְגַלְגְּלִין זְכוּת לְיוֹם זַכַּאי, וְחוֹבָה לְיוֹם חַיָּיב.

b17.he: אָמְרוּ: כְּשֶׁחָרַב הַבַּיִת בָּרִאשׁוֹנָה, אוֹתוֹ הַיּוֹם תִּשְׁעָה בְּאָב הָיָה, וּמוֹצָאֵי שַׁבָּת הָיָה, וּמוֹצָאֵי שְׁבִיעִית הָיְתָה, וּמִשְׁמַרְתּוֹ שֶׁל יְהוֹיָרִיב הָיְתָה, וְהָיוּ כֹּהֲנִים וּלְוִיִּם עוֹמְדִים עַל דּוּכָנָן וְאוֹמְרִים שִׁירָה, וּמָה שִׁירָה אָמְרוּ? ״וַיָּשֶׁב עֲלֵיהֶם אֶת אוֹנָם וּבְרָעָתָם יַצְמִיתֵם״, וְלֹא הִסְפִּיקוּ לוֹמַר ״יַצְמִיתֵם ה׳ אֱלֹהֵינוּ״ עַד שֶׁבָּאוּ גּוֹיִם וּכְבָשׁוּם, וְכֵן בַּשְּׁנִיָּה.

b18.he: הַאי שִׁירָה מַאי עֲבִידְתַּיהּ? אִילֵּימָא דְּעוֹלַת חוֹבָה, מִי הֲוַאי? בְּשִׁבְעָה עָשָׂר בְּתַמּוּז בָּטַל הַתָּמִיד! אֶלָּא לָאו דְּעוֹלַת נְדָבָה.

b19.he: וְתִסְבְּרַאּ?! מַאי שְׁנָא דְּעוֹלַת חוֹבָה דְּלָא הֲוַאי, וּמַאי שְׁנָא דְּעוֹלַת נְדָבָה דַּהֲוַאי? הָא לָא קַשְׁיָא: בֶּן בָּקָר אַקְרַאי בְּעָלְמָא הוּא דְּאִיתְרְמִיא לְהוּ.

b20.he: אָמַר רָבָא, וְאִיתֵּימָא רַב אָשֵׁי: וְתִסְבְּרָא, שִׁירָה דְּיוֹמֵיהּ ״לַה׳ הָאָרֶץ וּמְלוֹאָהּ״, וַיָּשֶׁב עֲלֵיהֶם אֶת אוֹנָם — בְּשִׁיר דְּאַרְבְּעָה בְּשַׁבָּת הוּא! אֶלָּא אִילְיָיא בְּעָלְמָא הוּא דִּנְפַל לְהוּ בְּפוּמַּיְיהוּ.

b21.he: וְהָא ״עוֹמְדִין עַל דּוּכָנָן״ קָתָנֵי! כִּדְרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ, דְּאָמַר: אוֹמֵר שֶׁלֹּא עַל הַקׇּרְבָּן. אִי הָכִי, בְּעוֹלַת נְדָבָה נָמֵי לֵימָא? נָפֵיק מִינַּהּ חוּרְבָּא.

b22.he: מַאי הֲוָה עֲלַהּ? תָּא שְׁמַע, דְּתָנֵי רַב מָרִי בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב כָּהֲנָא: ״עַל עֹלֹתֵיכֶם וְעַל זִבְחֵי שַׁלְמֵיכֶם״.

b23.he: מָה עוֹלָה קוֹדֶשׁ קָדָשִׁים — אַף שְׁלָמִים קוֹדֶשׁ קֳדָשִׁים, וּמָה שְׁלָמִים קָבוּעַ לָהֶם זְמַן — אַף עוֹלָה קָבוּעַ לָהּ זְמַן.

messages.text: Continued from 10b, on the mishna’s list of the Temple’s instruments: Rava bar Sheila said that Rav Mattana said that Shmuel said: There was a magreifa in the Temple.
There were ten holes in it and each and every one would emit ten types of tone. It therefore emerges that the entire instrument emitted one hundred types of tone.

notes.he: ובכל נקב היה קנה אחד ובכל קנה וקנה היו בו י' נקבים ובכל נקב של קנה הוציא מין זמר נמצאת כולה מוציאה מאה מיני זמר:
notes.en: There were ten holes in it: and in each hole there was one pipe, and in each and every pipe there were ten holes, and from each hole of a pipe it produced a type of tune. It emerges that the whole of it produced one hundred types of tune.

notes.he: בקתה שחלולה היתה כולה:
notes.en: There were ten holes in it: in its handle, which was entirely hollow.

messages.text: The magreifa was one cubit wide and one cubit tall, and a handle protruded from it. It was hollow and there were ten holes in it and each one would produce one hundred types of tone. It therefore emerges that the entire instrument emitted one thousand types of tone.

And your mnemonic to remember which of these two statements was said by Shmuel and which was taught in a baraita is that the baraita expresses itself with exaggeration, as it is common for baraitot to exaggerate numbers.
messages.quote: emitted one thousand types of tone

notes.he: שלא תטעה מי אמר מאה מי אמר אלף:
notes.en: And your mnemonic: so that you will not err as to who said a hundred and who said a thousand.

notes.he: דרך משניות לשנות גוזמא כגון הנך דאמר בשחיטת חולין בפרק גיד הנשה (חולין דף צ:):
notes.en: A baraita [speaks in] exaggeration: it is the way of mishnayot to teach in exaggeration, such as those [statements] that [the Gemara] cites in [tractate] Ḥullin, in chapter Gid HaNasheh (Ḥullin 90b).

notes.he: המשנה החיצונה מוטעת לעולם:
notes.en: A baraita [speaks in] exaggeration: the external teaching [the baraita] always errs [i.e., overstates].

messages.text: § The mishna teaches that the Temple musicians were slaves of priests according to Rabbi Meir, whereas according to Rabbi Yosei they were Israelites of pure lineage, and according to Rabbi Ḥanina ben Antigonus they were Levites.

Let us say that they disagree about this; that the one who says they were slaves holds that the primary component of song in the Temple service is singing with the mouth, and the instrumental music was performed merely to sweeten the sound of the singing. Since the instrumental music is mere accompaniment, it could be performed by slaves.

notes.he: (מה) [השיר] שהיו הלוים אומרים בפיהם הוא עיקר שירה:
notes.en: The primary component of song is with the mouth: the song that the Levites would say with their mouths is the primary component of song.

messages.text: And the one who says that the musicians were Levites holds that the primary component of song in the Temple service is the music played with instruments. Therefore, the musicians had to be Levites, who were tasked with the song that was part of the Temple service.

And can you understand the disagreement in this manner? According to this suggestion, what does Rabbi Yosei, who says that the musicians were Israelites of pure lineage, hold? If he holds that the primary component of song in the Temple service is singing with the mouth, then it should be sufficient if slaves play the instruments. Why would he require Israelites of pure lineage? And if he holds that the primary component of song in the Temple service is the music played with instruments, we should require Levites to play the instruments.
messages.quote: the primary component of song in the Temple service is singing with the mouth

notes.he: דאמר ישראלים מיוחסים היו מאי קסבר אלא דכ"ע עיקר שירה בפה:
notes.en: Rabbi Yosei: who said they were Israelites of pure lineage, what does he hold? Rather, everyone [agrees that] the primary component of song is with the mouth.

notes.he: דאמר דישראלים היו מאי קסבר כו']:
notes.en: [And can you understand? Rabbi Yosei, who said they were Israelites, what does he hold? etc.]

messages.text: Actually, Rabbi Yosei holds that the primary component of song in the Temple service is singing with the mouth. And here, the tanna’im disagree about whether the musicians in the Temple may be elevated from the musical platform to the presumptive status of pure lineage with regard to marriage and eligibility to receive Levitical tithes.

notes.he: קשה בפרק החליל (סוכה נא.) קאמר דאי עיקר שירה בפה אין שיר של קרבן נמי דחי שבת וי"ט לעשותו בכלי וא"כ מתני' דקתני י"ב ימים החליל מכה מני וי"ל דודאי תנאי דמתניתין אית להו עיקר שירה בפה אבל איכא תנא דרבי יוסי בר יהודה התם דאמר דשיר בכלי (דקרבן) דחי שבת וי"ט ואתי רישא כוותיה:
notes.en: No, everyone [agrees that] the primary component of song is with the mouth: There is a difficulty. In chapter HeḤalil (Sukka 51a) it says that if the primary component of song is with the mouth, then the song of an offering does not override Shabbat and the festival in order to perform it with an instrument. If so, the mishna [there] that teaches “For twelve days [of the year] the flute plays” — whose view is it? One can say that certainly the tanna’im of our mishna hold that the primary component of song is with the mouth, but there is a tanna there, Rabbi Yosei bar Yehuda, who says that song with an instrument [for an offering] overrides Shabbat and the festival, and the first clause [of that mishna] accords with him.

messages.text: The one who says that the musicians were slaves holds that people cannot be elevated from the Temple musical platform to the presumptive status of pure lineage with regard to marriage and eligibility to receive tithes.
The one who says that the musicians were Levites holds that one elevates from the platform both to the presumptive status of pure lineage and eligibility to receive tithes.

notes.he: דמחזקינן ליה בחזקת לוי:
notes.en: Both for tithes: for we establish him in the presumptive status of a Levite.

notes.he: מעלין מדוכן בין ליוחסין בין למעשרות ומאי דחזי להו דקיימי בין לוים לא דייק אי בכלי מזמרין או בפה ומעלין ליוחסין ומחלקין להן מעשר:
notes.en: One elevates from the platform both to lineage and to tithes: and as for what they saw, that [these men] stood among the Levites, one does not examine whether they played with an instrument or [sang] with the mouth; one elevates [them] to lineage and distributes tithes to them.

messages.text: And according to the one who says that the musicians were Israelites, he holds that one elevates from the platform to the presumptive status of pure lineage but not with regard to the eligibility to receive tithes.

notes.he: משום הכי בעינן משיאין לכהונה:
notes.en: One elevates from the platform to lineage: therefore we require [families who may] marry into the priesthood.

notes.he: אבל לא למעשרות משום הכי לא בעינן לוים:
notes.en: But not to tithes: therefore we do not require Levites.

messages.caption: Who played in the Temple, and what serving on the platform proves about a family, according to the Gemara’s conclusion.

messages.text: The song that the Levites sing while a communal offering is being sacrificed is an indispensable component of the offering, which means that if the Levites did not sing, the offering is invalid. This is the statement of Rabbi Meir.

notes.he: קשה דהא השיר בשעת ניסוך והניסוך אין מעכבת הקרבן דאדם מביא זבחו היום ונסכים מכאן עד ארבעה ימים (מנחות דף טו:) ונראה לפרש שיר מעכב את הקרבן היינו ניסוך שאם אין שירה אין ניסוך:
notes.en: The song is indispensable to the offering: There is a difficulty, for the song is at the time of the libation, and the libation does not hold back the offering, for a person may bring his offering today and the libations from now until four days later (Menaḥot 15b). And it seems [right] to explain that “the song is indispensable to the offering” means [it is indispensable to] the libation: for if there is no song, there is no libation.

messages.text: It is not indispensable.
What is the reasoning of Rabbi Meir, i.e., from where does he derive his opinion?

It is as the verse states: “And I have given the Levites, they are given to Aaron and to his sons from among the children of Israel, to do the service of the children of Israel in the Tent of Meeting, and to make atonement for the children of Israel.” The verse compares the atonement for the Jewish people, which is caused by the sprinkling of the blood of offerings on the altar, to the service of the Levites, which is their singing. This teaches that just as the atonement caused by the sprinkling of the blood is an indispensable component of the offering, so too the song of the Levites is indispensable.

verse.he: וָאֶתְּנָה אֶת־הַלְוִיִּם נְתֻנִים ׀ לְאַהֲרֹן וּלְבָנָיו מִתּוֹךְ בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל לַעֲבֹד אֶת־עֲבֹדַת בְּנֵי־יִשְׂרָאֵל בְּאֹהֶל מוֹעֵד וּלְכַפֵּר עַל־בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל וְלֹא יִהְיֶה בִּבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל נֶגֶף בְּגֶשֶׁת בְּנֵי־יִשְׂרָאֵל אֶל־הַקֹּדֶשׁ׃
verse.en: and from among the Israelites I formally assign the Levites to Aaron and his sons, to perform the service for the Israelites in the Tent of Meeting and to make expiation for the Israelites, so that no plague may afflict the Israelites for coming too near the sanctuary.

notes.he: ולוים משוררים הם:
notes.en: And I have given the Levites: and the Levites are the singers.

notes.he: [לעבוד את עבודת בני ישראל באהל מועד:
notes.en: [“To do the service of the children of Israel in the Tent of Meeting,

notes.he: מה כפרה. דכהנים (מעכבת דהיינו מתן דמים אף עבודת הלוים דהיינו השירה מעכבת) [מתן דמים מעכבת אף שירה דלוים מעכבת. דהיינו עבודה דלוים]:
notes.en: and to make atonement”]: just as the atonement of the priests, that is, the placing of the blood, is indispensable, so too the service of the Levites, that is, the song, is indispensable.

messages.text: And what do the Rabbis derive from the comparison in this verse? That comparison serves to teach another halakha, which was stated by Rabbi Elazar,
Just as the atonement achieved by the sprinkling of the blood must take place during the day, so too the song must be sung during the day.

notes.he: להכי איתקש עבודה דלוים לכפרה דכהנים דמה כפרה ביום דכתיב ביום צוותו:
notes.en: And the Rabbis: for this [purpose] the service of the Levites is juxtaposed to the atonement of the priests: just as atonement is by day, as it is written “on the day that He commanded” (Leviticus 7:38) [so too song is by day].

messages.text: From where is it derived that the basic requirement to accompany communal offerings with song applies by Torah law? As it is stated with regard to a Levite who serves in the Temple: “Then he shall serve with the name of the Lord his God.” What is this service that is performed with the name of God? You must say that this is the song, in which the Levites mention and praise the name of God.

verse.he: וְשֵׁרֵת בְּשֵׁם יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהָיו כְּכׇל־אֶחָיו הַלְוִיִּם הָעֹמְדִים שָׁם לִפְנֵי יְהֹוָה׃
verse.en: He may serve in the name of the ETERNAL his God like all his fellow Levites who are there in attendance before GOD.

notes.he: שמזכירין בו שם שמים: אין אדם שר שירה אלא מתוך שמחה וטוב לבב דכתיב (ישעיהו ס״ה:י״ד) הנה עבדי ירונו מטוב לב:
notes.en: That is with the Name: in which they mention the name of Heaven. A person sings song only out of joy and goodness of heart, as it is written: “Behold, My servants shall sing for goodness of heart” (Isaiah 65:14).

notes.he: שמזכיר בה את השם:
notes.en: [Service] that is with the Name: in which one mentions the Name.

notes.he: אזכרות שבמזמורים [היינו שירה שיש במזמורות אזכרות]:
notes.en: This is song: the mentions [of God’s name] in the psalms; [that is, song, for there are mentions of the Name in the psalms].

messages.text: But you can say that this service with the name of God is referring to the lifting of the hands for the Priestly Benediction, which also includes the mention of the name of God. If so, the verse is referring to priests, not ordinary Levites.
messages.quote: What is this service that is performed with the name of God?

notes.he: דכהנים שיש בה הזכרות השם דפשטיה דהאי קרא בכהנים כתיב דגמרינן מיניה בזמן שי"ט סמוך לשבת בין מלפניה בין מאחריה היו כל המשמרות שוין בחילוק לחם הפנים שנאמר וכי יבא הלוי מאחד שעריך מאי שעריך בשעה שכל ישראל נכנסין בשער אחד. וכתיב חלק כחלק יאכלו:
notes.en: But say the lifting of the hands: of the priests, in which there is mention of the Name, since the plain sense of this verse is written about priests, for we derive from it that when a festival falls next to Shabbat, whether before it or after it, all the priestly watches were equal in dividing the shewbread, as it is said: “And if a Levite comes from any of your gates” (Deuteronomy 18:6). What is “your gates”? The time when all Israel enter through one gate. And it is written: “They shall have like portions to eat” (Deuteronomy 18:8).

messages.text: From the fact that it is written: “At that time the Lord separated the tribe of Levi…to serve Him, and to bless in His name,” it can be derived by inference that the Priestly Benediction is not considered service, as the verse mentions service and the Priestly Benediction as distinct rituals.

verse.he: בָּעֵת הַהִוא הִבְדִּיל יְהֹוָה אֶת־שֵׁבֶט הַלֵּוִי לָשֵׂאת אֶת־אֲרוֹן בְּרִית־יְהֹוָה לַעֲמֹד לִפְנֵי יְהֹוָה לְשָׁרְתוֹ וּלְבָרֵךְ בִּשְׁמוֹ עַד הַיּוֹם הַזֶּה׃
verse.en: At that time GOD set apart the tribe of Levi to carry the Ark of GOD’s Covenant, to stand in attendance upon GOD, and to bless in God’s name, as is still the case.

messages.text: The source for the requirement to accompany the Temple offerings with song is derived from here: “Because you did not serve the Lord your God with joyfulness, and with goodness of heart.” What is this service of God that is performed with joyfulness and with goodness of heart? You must say that this is song.

verse.he: תַּחַת אֲשֶׁר לֹא־עָבַדְתָּ אֶת־יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ בְּשִׂמְחָה וּבְטוּב לֵבָב מֵרֹב כֹּל׃
verse.en: Because you would not serve the ETERNAL your God in joy and gladness over the abundance of everything,

notes.he: הוי אומר זו שירה דכתיב עבדי ירונו מטוב לב:
notes.en: You must say this is song, as it is written: “My servants shall sing for goodness of heart” (Isaiah 65:14).

messages.text: But you can say that this service is studying the words of Torah, as it is written: “The precepts of the Lord are upright, rejoicing the heart.”
messages.quote: with joyfulness and with goodness of heart

verse.he: פִּקּוּדֵי יְהֹוָה יְשָׁרִים מְשַׂמְּחֵי־לֵב מִצְוַת יְהֹוָה בָּרָה מְאִירַת עֵינָיִם׃
verse.en:
The precepts of GOD are just,
rejoicing the heart;
the instruction of GOD is lucid,
making the eyes light up.

messages.text: Torah is indeed called a matter that rejoices the heart, but it is not called “goodness.”

notes.dh: משמח לב איקרי טוב לא איקרי
notes.he: וא"ת והכתיב (משלי ד) לקח טוב נתתי לכם (תהלים קיט) טוב לי תורת פיך וי"ל דה"ק משמח לב איקרי טוב שסמוך (ללב) לשמחה ומשמעותו לשון שמחה א"נ טוב הסמוך ללב לא איקרי וא"ת והא כתיב (רות ג) וייטב לבו ופירש"י שיש במדרש וייטב לבו בתלמוד תורה וה"נ דרשינן שבת (דף סג:) ויטיבך לבך על תלמוד תורה וי"ל דלא כתיבי בהדיא ולפ"ז לא הוי אתי שפיר הא דמקשה ואימא ביכורים דהא טוב סמוך ללב לא איקרו וי"ל דה"נ משני דבעינן טוב הסמוך ללב ומיהו כיון דהיה יודע דבעינן טוב הסמוך ללב מעיקרא שוב לא צריך להקשות עוד מביכורים ולשון ראשון עיקר:
notes.en: It is called “rejoicing the heart”; it is not called “goodness”: And if you say: But isn’t it written [of Torah]: “For I give you good doctrine” (Proverbs 4:2), and “The Torah of Your mouth is good to me” (Psalms 119:72)? One can say that this is what it means: it is called “rejoicing the heart,” [but] “goodness” placed next to joy, so that its meaning is an expression of joy, it is not called. Alternatively: “goodness” placed next to “heart” it is not called. And if you say: But isn’t it written: “And his heart was merry [vayitav libo]” (Ruth 3:7), and Rashi explained that the midrash has: his heart was merry with Torah study; and likewise we expound in Shabbat (63b) “Let your heart cheer you [vitivkha libkha]” as referring to Torah study? One can say that these are not written explicitly. And according to this [second explanation], the objection “But say first fruits” does not fit well, since they are not called “goodness placed next to heart.” One can say that indeed this is what [the Gemara] answers, that we require goodness placed next to heart. However, since it already knew from the outset that we require goodness placed next to heart, it should not have needed to object again from first fruits. And the first explanation is the main one.

messages.text: But you can say that the joyful service of God referred to above is the bringing of the first fruits, as it is written in that context: “And you shall rejoice in all the goodness” that the Lord your God has given you.

verse.he: וְשָׂמַחְתָּ בְכׇל־הַטּוֹב אֲשֶׁר נָתַן־לְךָ יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ וּלְבֵיתֶךָ אַתָּה וְהַלֵּוִי וְהַגֵּר אֲשֶׁר בְּקִרְבֶּךָ׃ {ס}
verse.en: And you shall enjoy, together with the Levite and the stranger in your midst, all the bounty that the ETERNAL your God has bestowed upon you and your household.

notes.he: וה"ק קרא תחת אשר לא הבאת ביכורים:
notes.en: But say first fruits: and this is what the verse means: because you did not bring first fruits.

messages.text: Bringing the first fruits is indeed called goodness, but it is not called something that involves goodness of heart.

notes.he: לא תורה ולא ביכורים:
notes.en: It is not called goodness of heart: neither Torah nor first fruits.

messages.text: From where is it derived that bringing the first fruits to the Temple requires the accompaniment of song? It is derived from here, i.e., from the requirement to accompany communal offerings with song, by means of a verbal analogy of the word goodness in the verse “And with goodness of heart” and the word goodness in the verse “You shall rejoice in all the goodness.”

notes.he: שאומרים ארוממך ה' כי דליתני כדתנן במס' ביכורים (פ"ג מ"ד):
notes.en: From where [is it derived] that first fruits require song: for they say “I will extol You, Lord, for You have drawn me up” (Psalms 30:2), as we learned in tractate Bikkurim (3:4).

notes.he: כתיב הכא בכל הטוב וכתיב בשירה (דברים כ״ח:מ״ז) בשמחה ובטוב לבב:
notes.en: Goodness, goodness: here [with regard to first fruits] it is written “in all the goodness,” and with regard to song it is written (Deuteronomy 28:47): “with joyfulness and with goodness of heart.”

notes.he: פרש"י (דתנא) שהיו טעונין שירה [כדתנן במס' ביכורים] (פ"ג מ"ד) החליל (היה) מכה לפניהם [כו'] והא דפריך איני והא אמר ר' שמואל בר נחמני ומקשה לרבי שמואל בר נחמני אך יש תימה אמאי לא מקשה ליה בהדיא מן המשנה וי"ל שהש"ס לא הביא המשנה דזרעים וגם מילתיה דר' שמואל בר נחמני לא אייתי ליה הש"ס אלא אגב גררא הלכך לא פריך אלא הכי ולרבי נראה ששיר המשנה על ביכורים אינו עיקר השיר כ"א לשמחה בעלמא הלכך לא פריך מינה לר' שמואל בר נחמני ולא כפירש"י ויש תימה דלא איירי המשנה בעיקר שיר כלל ועוד הקשה ר' אלחנן היכי מוקי לה למשנת ביכורים הכא בהביא ענבים ודרכן דהא בכל הביכורים מיירי בתאנים וחטין וכל ז' המינין ואין לפרש דה"ק שאם הביא ענבים בביכורים ודרכן לאחר כך שלא תפקע מהם קדושת הביכורים אע"ג דכתיב בקרא פרי דהתם תניא בחולין פרק העור והרוטב (חולין דף קכ:) אין מביאין ביכורים משקה אלא היוצא מן הזיתים ומן הענבים אלמא שהמשקה מהם חשוב לביכורים אלא דיש לפרש הביא ענבים ודרכם פי' הפריש ענבים ודרכם מנין שכשרים לביכורים ת"ל תביא והא דתניא אין מביאין ביכורים משקה אלא היוצא מן הזיתים ומן הענבים דמשמע לכתחילה מביאין יש לפרשו בדיעבד דהא קרא כתיב שאומרים שיר על ביכורים והיכי כתב קרא בדיעבד ונראה לפרש דמיירי לכתחלה וה"פ הביא ענבים ודרכן מנין שיביאם לכתחילה ת"ל תביא דמשמע לכתחילה ומשנת ביכורים נמי אתיא שפיר דמיירי במשקין היוצאין מזיתים וענבים שאומרים עליהם שירה לכתחילה ואיידי דתקנו עליהם שירה תקנו נמי בכל הביכורים של ז' המינים ולא קשיא מידי מכל מה שהקשיתי לעיל וצ"ע בירושלמי:
notes.en: In brief: From where [is it derived] that first fruits require song: Rashi explains that they required song, as the mishna in Bikkurim (3:4) teaches that the flute played before those bringing them; the Gemara’s challenge “Is that so? But Rabbi Shmuel bar Naḥmani said…” is then a challenge to Rabbi Shmuel bar Naḥmani. Question: why not challenge him directly from that mishna? Answer: the Talmud does not cite the mishna of the order Zera’im, and Rabbi Shmuel bar Naḥmani’s statement is brought only incidentally. Our teacher holds instead, against Rashi, that the song in the Bikkurim mishna is not the essential song but only for joy, which is why the Gemara does not challenge him from it; and it is puzzling [for Rashi], since that mishna does not speak of the essential song at all. Rabbi Elḥanan further asked: how can the Gemara set the Bikkurim mishna in a case of one who brought grapes and pressed them, when it speaks of all first fruits, figs, wheat and all seven species? One cannot explain that the question is whether grapes brought and then pressed keep their sanctity as first fruits, since Ḥullin (120b) teaches that one brings first fruits as liquid only from olives and grapes, so liquid from them clearly counts. One might explain that he set aside grapes and pressed them, and “you shall bring” teaches they are fit; and the baraita that one brings liquid only from olives and grapes would mean after the fact. But the verse is the source for saying song over first fruits, and how would it speak of an after-the-fact case? So Tosafot explain that it speaks of bringing them so from the outset: “you shall bring” teaches that one may bring pressed grapes ab initio, and the Bikkurim mishna fits too, since it speaks of the liquids of olives and grapes, over which song is said from the outset; and once song was instituted over them, it was instituted over all first fruits of the seven species. None of the earlier difficulties remain, and the matter requires examination in the Jerusalem Talmud. Open on Sefaria for the full text.

notes.he: כתיב בשירה ובטוב לבב. ובביכורים בכל הטוב:
notes.en: It is derived [from] goodness, goodness: it is written with regard to song “and with goodness of heart,” and with regard to first fruits “in all the goodness.”

messages.text: Is that so?
messages.quote: first fruits to the Temple requires the accompaniment of song

messages.text: From where is it derived that songs of praise in the Temple are recited only over the wine libation accompanying the sacrifice? As it is stated: “And the vine replied: Should I leave my wine, which gladdens God and man,” and go and wave above the trees. If it is clear that wine gladdens people, in what way does it gladden God? Rather, derive from here that songs of praise in the Temple are recited only over the wine of libation, and it is this song that gladdens God.
messages.lead: But doesn’t Rabbi Shmuel bar Naḥmani say that Rabbi Yonatan said:

verse.he: וַתֹּאמֶר לָהֶם הַגֶּפֶן הֶחֳדַלְתִּי אֶת־תִּירוֹשִׁי הַמְשַׂמֵּחַ אֱלֹהִים וַאֲנָשִׁים וְהָלַכְתִּי לָנוּעַ עַל־הָעֵצִים׃
verse.en: But the vine replied, ‘Have I stopped yielding my new wine, which gladdens God and humans, that I should go and wave above the trees?’

notes.he: לוים שירה אלא על היין בשעת ניסוך היין [שנאמר ותאמר להם הגפן וגו']:
notes.en: From where that [the Levites] recite song only over wine: at the time of the wine libation, [as it is said: “And the vine said to them,” etc.].

messages.text: This is difficult, as since there is no wine libation associated with the bringing of first fruits, how can it be accompanied by song?
You can find cases where the first fruits are brought in the form of wine,
messages.quote: songs of praise in the Temple are recited only over the wine

notes.he: אפי' לר' יונתן [דאמר] דאומר שירה על הביכורים:
notes.en: You can find it: even according to Rabbi Yonatan, that one says song over first fruits.

messages.text: The verse states with regard to the first fruits: “You shall take of the first of all the fruit of the ground, which you shall bring in from your land.” Since the verse mentions “fruit,” you must bring the actual fruit as your first fruits offering, and you may not bring it in the form of beverages. If one brought grapes and he had already pressed them into wine, from where is it derived that he has fulfilled his obligation of offering his first fruits? The verse states: “You shall bring in from your land.” This apparently superfluous phrase comes to teach that if one brings wine for the mitzva of first fruits, he has fulfilled his obligation.

verse.he: וְלָקַחְתָּ מֵרֵאשִׁית ׀ כׇּל־פְּרִי הָאֲדָמָה אֲשֶׁר תָּבִיא מֵאַרְצְךָ אֲשֶׁר יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ נֹתֵן לָךְ וְשַׂמְתָּ בַטֶּנֶא וְהָלַכְתָּ אֶל־הַמָּקוֹם אֲשֶׁר יִבְחַר יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֶיךָ לְשַׁכֵּן שְׁמוֹ שָׁם׃
verse.en: you shall take some of every first fruit of the soil, which you harvest from the land that the ETERNAL your God is giving you, put it in a basket and go to the place where the ETERNAL your God will choose to establish the divine name.

notes.he: בביכורים כתיב (שם כו) מראשית פרי:
notes.en: Fruit: with regard to first fruits it is written (Deuteronomy 26:2): “of the first of all the fruit.”

notes.he: לעזרה לביכורים ודרכן מנין שיצא ת"ל אשר תביא מארצך מ"מ:
notes.en: He brought grapes: to the Temple courtyard as first fruits, and pressed them: from where [is it derived] that he has fulfilled [his obligation]? The verse states: “which you shall bring in from your land,” in any case.

notes.he: כדתני רב יוסף [שהן יין]:
notes.en: As Rav Yosef teaches [that they are wine]. [The daf reads “Rabbi Yosei”; Rabbeinu Gershom’s text reads “Rav Yosef.”]

notes.he: (מנין שאם) הביא ענבים בכורים לירושלים ודרכן קודם ביאתו לעזרה מנין שטעון הבאה אותו יין ת"ל תביא לרבות:
notes.en: (From where that if) he brought grapes as first fruits to Jerusalem and pressed them before he came to the Temple courtyard, from where [is it derived] that it requires bringing as that wine? The verse states “you shall bring,” to include [it].

messages.text: This obligation is derived from here: “And Chenaniah, chief of the Levites…he was master of lifting, because he was skillful.” Do not read it as “he was master [yasor] of lifting,” but as: He shall sing [yashir] with the lifting of his voice.

verse.he: וּכְנַנְיָהוּ שַׂר־הַלְוִיִּם בְּמַשָּׂא יָסֹר בַּמַּשָּׂא כִּי מֵבִין הוּא׃
verse.en: also Chenaniah, officer of the Levites in song; he was in charge of the song because he was a master.

notes.he: אשכחן שירת לוים מן התורה ישור במשא נשיאות קול בשיר:
notes.en: (He was master of lifting) Ḥizkiyya said from here: we have found [a source for] the Levites’ song from the Torah. “He was master of lifting [yasor bamassa]”: the lifting of the voice in song.

notes.he: תימה דכמה קראי איכא בדברי הימים (א ט) בני פלוני משוררים וי"ל דבעי לאשכוחי דשירה מן התורה לכך דייק ליה מהך קרא דכתיב ישור במשא וכתיב עבודת משא אי נמי מפיק מקראי שהיא עבודה וזר חייב עליה מיתה:
notes.en: Do not read yasor but yashir: It is puzzling, for there are many verses in Chronicles (I Chronicles 9) [saying] that the sons of so-and-so were singers. One can say that he needs to find that song is from the Torah; therefore he infers it from this verse, where it is written “yasor bamassa” [lifting], and [in the Torah] it is written “the service of bearing [massa]” (Numbers 4:47). Alternatively, he derives from [these] verses that it is a service, so that a non-Levite [lit. stranger] is liable to death for it.

notes.he: הוי לשון שררה:
notes.en: Yasor bamassa: it is an expression of authority [serara].

messages.text: The requirement for the Levites to accompany the Temple offerings with song is derived from here: The verse states with regard to the Levites: “Every one that entered in to do the work of service.” What is work that must be performed in conjunction with another service? You must say that this is song.

verse.he: מִבֶּן שְׁלֹשִׁים שָׁנָה וָמַעְלָה וְעַד בֶּן־חֲמִשִּׁים שָׁנָה כׇּל־הַבָּא לַעֲבֹד עֲבֹדַת עֲבֹדָה וַעֲבֹדַת מַשָּׂא בְּאֹהֶל מוֹעֵד׃
verse.en: from the age of thirty years up to the age of fifty, all who were subject to duties of service and porterage relating to the Tent of Meeting—

notes.he: שם חכם:
notes.en: Balvatei: the name of a sage.

notes.he: צריך עבודת קרבן שאינו נאמר אלא על היין של נסכי קרבן כדכתיב (במדבר י׳:י׳) ותקעתם בחצוצרות על עולותיכם:
notes.en: Song: [is the work that] requires the service of an offering, for it is said only over the wine of the offering’s libations, as it is written (Numbers 10:10): “And you shall blow with the trumpets over your burnt offerings.”

notes.he: שם חכם:
notes.en: (Yashir) [Balvatei: the name of a sage.

notes.he: הוי אומר זה שיר. שהלוים אומרים בפה ואחרים עובדים להם בכלי שיר ומסייעין להם:
notes.en: What is service that requires service]: you must say this is song, which the Levites say with the mouth, while others serve them with musical instruments and assist them.

notes.he: ואיכא דאמרי שצריכה עבודה דאין אומרים שירה אלא בשעת עבודה:
notes.en: And some say: [work] that requires service, for one recites song only at the time of the service [of the offering].

messages.text: The requirement to accompany the Temple offerings with song is derived from here: “Sing aloud to God…Take up the melody, and sound the timbrel, the sweet harp with the lyre.”

verse.he: הַרְנִינוּ לֵאלֹהִים עוּזֵּנוּ הָרִיעוּ לֵאלֹהֵי יַעֲקֹב׃ שְׂאוּ־זִמְרָה וּתְנוּ־תֹף כִּנּוֹר נָעִים עִם־נָבֶל׃
verse.en:
Sing joyously to God, our strength;
raise a shout for the God of Jacob. Take up the song,
sound the hand-drum,
the melodious lyre and harp.

messages.text: The obligation is derived from here: “Those yonder lift up their voice, they sing for joy; for the majesty of the Lord they shout from the sea.”

verse.he: הֵמָּה יִשְׂאוּ קוֹלָם יָרֹנּוּ בִּגְאוֹן יְהֹוָה צָהֲלוּ מִיָּם׃
verse.en:
These shall lift up their voices,
Exult in GOD’s majesty.
They shall shout from the sea:

notes.he: יצהלו בשיר בית המקדש יותר מצהלת ים סוף:
notes.en: They shout from the sea: they will shout in song in the Temple more than the shouting at the Red Sea.

messages.text: “But unto the sons of Kohath he gave none, because the service of the holy things belonged to them: They bore them [yisa’u] upon their shoulders.”
messages.lead: And a tanna cites a derivation for the requirement for the Levites to accompany the Temple offerings with song from here:

verse.he: וְלִבְנֵי קְהָת לֹא נָתָן כִּי־עֲבֹדַת הַקֹּדֶשׁ עֲלֵהֶם בַּכָּתֵף יִשָּׂאוּ׃
verse.en: But to the Kohathites he did not give any; since theirs was the service of the [most] sacred objects, their porterage was by shoulder.

notes.he: לעיקר שירה מן התורה:
notes.en: Cites it from here: [the source for] the basic requirement of song from the Torah.

messages.text: By inference from that which is stated, “upon their shoulders,” don’t I know that they bore them? Why must the verse state “yisa’u”? The term “yisa’u” is not stated here in its meaning of “they bore them,” but rather as an expression of song. And similarly, the verse states: “Take up [se’u] the melody, and sound the timbrel,” and another verse states: “They lift up [yisu] their voice, they sing for joy.”
The requirement for the Levites to sing in the Temple is derived from here: “Moses spoke, and God answered him with a voice”

verse.he: וַיְהִי קוֹל הַשֹּׁפָר הוֹלֵךְ וְחָזֵק מְאֹד מֹשֶׁה יְדַבֵּר וְהָאֱלֹהִים יַעֲנֶנּוּ בְקוֹל׃
verse.en: The blare of the horn grew louder and louder. As Moses spoke, God answered him in thunder.

messages.text: This indicates that God responded to Moses, who was a Levite, by commanding him about matters pertaining to the voice, i.e., that the Levites must accompany the sacrifices with song.

notes.he: שהיה מצוהו לשורר לפי שמשה לוי היה:
notes.en: About matters of voice: that He was commanding him to sing, since Moses was a Levite.

notes.he: בשעה שהיה משה משורר שהוא לוי האלהים יעננו לו בקול:
notes.en: About matters of voice: when Moses, who was a Levite, would sing, God would answer him with a voice.

messages.text: The obligation for the Levites to sing in the Temple is derived from here: “It came to pass, when the trumpeters and singers were as one, to make one sound” to be heard in praising and thanking the Lord. This indicates that just as there is a requirement for trumpets to be sounded during the sacrifice of communal offerings (see Numbers 10:10), there is likewise a requirement for the Levites to sing.

verse.he: וַיְהִי כְאֶחָד (למחצצרים) [לַמְחַצְּרִים] וְלַמְשֹׁרְרִים לְהַשְׁמִיעַ קוֹל־אֶחָד לְהַלֵּל וּלְהֹדוֹת לַיהֹוָה וּכְהָרִים קוֹל בַּחֲצֹצְרוֹת וּבִמְצִלְתַּיִם וּבִכְלֵי הַשִּׁיר וּבְהַלֵּל לַיהֹוָה כִּי טוֹב כִּי לְעוֹלָם חַסְדּוֹ וְהַבַּיִת מָלֵא עָנָן בֵּית יְהֹוָה׃
verse.en: The trumpeters and the singers joined in unison to praise and extol GOD; and as the sound of the trumpets, cymbals, and other musical instruments, and the praise of GOD, “who is good—and whose steadfast love is eternal,” grew louder, the House, the House of GOD, was filled with a cloud.

notes.he: ובקרא (במדבר י׳:י׳) כתיב ותקעתם בחצוצרות על עולותיכם אלמא איכא שירה [מן התורה]:
notes.en: From here: “It came to pass, when the trumpeters [and singers] were as one”: and in the verse (Numbers 10:10) it is written: “And you shall blow with the trumpets over your burnt offerings.” Evidently there is song [from the Torah].

messages.text: The requirement for the Levites to sing in the Temple is derived from here: The Torah commands the priests with regard to the Levites: “They shall not come near the altar, that they die not, neither they nor you.” The verse equates the Levites with the priests, indicating that just as you, the priests, are obligated to perform the service on the altar, so too they, the Levites, are obligated to perform a service pertaining to the altar, i.e., the song that accompanies the offerings.

verse.he: וְשָׁמְרוּ מִשְׁמַרְתְּךָ וּמִשְׁמֶרֶת כׇּל־הָאֹהֶל אַךְ אֶל־כְּלֵי הַקֹּדֶשׁ וְאֶל־הַמִּזְבֵּחַ לֹא יִקְרָבוּ וְלֹא־יָמֻתוּ גַם־הֵם גַּם־אַתֶּם׃
verse.en: They shall discharge their duties to you and to the Tent as a whole, but they must not have any contact with the furnishings of the Shrine or with the altar, lest both they and you die.

notes.he: הלוים בעבודת מזבח ולא משכחת לוים כשרים בעבודת מזבח אלא בשיר:
notes.en: So too they: the Levites, in the service of the altar; and you do not find Levites fit for the service of the altar except in song.

notes.he: אכהנים קאי קרא:
notes.en: Just as you: the verse is addressed to the priests.

notes.he: שירה בשעת קרבן:
notes.en: So too they in the service of the altar: song at the time of the offering.

messages.text: It is stated: “That they die not, neither they nor you.” This indicates that if you, the priests, perform their duties, i.e., the Levites’ duties, or they, the Levites, perform yours, e.g., the sacrificial rites, the perpetrator is liable to receive death at the hand of Heaven.
messages.lead: A derivation of halakhot based on the comparison between priests and Levites in this verse is also taught in a baraita:

notes.he: הכהנים שנכנסו בעבודת לוים כגון ששררו:
notes.en: You in theirs: priests who entered into the service of the Levites, for example, that they sang.

notes.he: לוי שעבד על המזבח ככהן:
notes.en: And they in yours: a Levite who served at the altar like a priest.

notes.he: כלומר אם שינו עבודתן לוי לכהן הרי הן במיתה:
notes.en: You in theirs: that is, if they switched their service, a Levite for a priest, they are [liable] to death.

messages.text: But if they, the Levites, perform a function that belongs to a different group of Levites, but is nevertheless a duty of theirs, i.e., the Levites in general, e.g., if Levites assigned to open and close the gates of the Temple decide instead to sing, they are not punished with death; rather, they have merely violated a prohibition.

notes.he: כגון לוי משורר שהגיף דלתות ולוי משוער שאמר שיר שהרי הלוים היו חלוקים זה למשוער וזה למשורר:
notes.en: They in theirs: for example, a Levite singer who closed the doors, or a Levite gatekeeper who sang song, for the Levites were divided, this one to be a gatekeeper and that one to be a singer.

notes.he: לא אתפרש לן:
notes.en: But only with a prohibition: [its source] has not been explained to us.

notes.he: כלומר ששינו עבודת' כגון שוער ששרר או משורר ששיער אינן אלא באזהרה בלאו:
notes.en: They in theirs: that is, they switched their service, for example a gatekeeper who sang or a singer who served as a gatekeeper; it is only a warning, a negative prohibition.

messages.text: We hold that a Levite designated to serve as a singer who instead served in another Levite’s position as a gatekeeper is liable to be put to death, as it is stated: “And those that were to pitch tent before the Tabernacle eastward, before the Tent of Meeting toward the sunrising, were Moses and Aaron and his sons, keeping the charge of the Sanctuary, for the charge of the children of Israel; and the stranger that drew near was to be put to death.”
messages.quote: they are not punished with death; rather, they have merely violated a prohibition

verse.he: וְהַחֹנִים לִפְנֵי הַמִּשְׁכָּן קֵדְמָה לִפְנֵי אֹהֶל־מוֹעֵד ׀ מִזְרָחָה מֹשֶׁה ׀ וְאַהֲרֹן וּבָנָיו שֹׁמְרִים מִשְׁמֶרֶת הַמִּקְדָּשׁ לְמִשְׁמֶרֶת בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל וְהַזָּר הַקָּרֵב יוּמָת׃
verse.en: Those who were to camp before the Tabernacle, in front—before the Tent of Meeting, on the east—were Moses and Aaron and his sons, attending to the duties of the sanctuary, as a duty on behalf of the Israelites; and any outsider who encroached was to be put to death.

notes.he: לית ליה הא מתני' דקתני לעיל הם בשלהם אינו במיתה דהא משכחת תנא אחרינא דקאי כוותיה:
notes.en: Abaye: does not hold of this baraita taught above, “they in theirs are not [liable] to death,” since he finds another tanna who holds as he does.

messages.text: What is the meaning of the term “stranger” in this verse? If we say it is referring to an actual stranger, i.e., a non-Levite, isn’t it written already on another occasion that he is liable to be put to death (see Numbers 3:10)? Rather, this is not its meaning; instead, it is referring to one who is a Levite but is a stranger to that service.

notes.he: כגון ישראל:
notes.en: An actual stranger: for example, an Israelite.

notes.he: בההיא פרשתא גופה וקאי נמי אעבודת לוים:
notes.en: Isn’t it written once: in that very passage itself, and it too refers to the service of the Levites.

notes.he: הא כתיב חדא זימנא ואת אהרן ואת בניו תפקוד ושמרו את כהונתם והזר הקרב יומת משוער היינו שומר השערים כדכת' וחוסה על השערים:
notes.en: Isn’t it written once: “And you shall appoint Aaron and his sons, and they shall keep their priesthood; and the stranger that draws near shall be put to death” (Numbers 3:10). A gatekeeper is the guard of the gates, as it is written: “and watches over the gates.” [We could not locate this last phrase as a verse.]

messages.text: The Gemara raises an objection to Abaye’s statement from a baraita:
messages.quote: a singer who instead served in another Levite’s position as a gatekeeper is liable to be put to death

messages.text: A singer who served as a gatekeeper and a gatekeeper who sang are not punished with death; rather, they have merely violated a prohibition.

notes.he: דבדברי הימים (א ט) כתיב משפחות שהיו משוערים ומשפחות שהיו משוררים:
notes.en: A gatekeeper who sang: for in Chronicles (I Chronicles 9) it is written that there were families who were gatekeepers and families who were singers.

notes.he: פ"ה לא ידענא האי אזהרה מהיכא היא ורבינו מנחם נ"ע פי' דכתיב (במדבר ח׳:כ״ו) לשמור משמרת ועבודה לא יעבוד וכתיב (שם) ככה תעשה ללוים במשמרותם:
notes.en: Raises an objection: Rashi explained: I do not know where this prohibition comes from. And Rabbeinu Menaḥem, may his soul rest in Eden, explained: for it is written: “to keep the charge, but he shall do no service” (Numbers 8:26), and it is written there: “Thus shall you do to the Levites with regard to their charges.”

messages.text: This matter is a dispute between tanna’im, as it is taught in a baraita:
There was an incident involving Rabbi Yehoshua bar Ḥananya, a Levite, who went to Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Gudgeda, also a Levite, in order to assist in closing the doors of the Temple.

notes.he: רבי יהושע ויוחנן בן גודגדא לוים היו. יוחנן בן גודגדא סבר משורר ששוער במיתה כשהוא מגיף לבדו וגזרו רבנן במסייע דלא ליתי למעבד לחודיה ור' יהושע סבר אפילו כי עביד לחודיה אינו אלא באזהרה ולא גזרו רבנן במסייע:
notes.en: Rabbi Yehoshua and Yoḥanan ben Gudgeda were Levites. Yoḥanan ben Gudgeda holds that a singer who served as a gatekeeper is [liable] to death when he closes [the doors] by himself, and the Rabbis decreed against one who assists, lest he come to do it by himself. And Rabbi Yehoshua holds that even when he does it by himself it is only a prohibition, and the Rabbis did not decree against one who assists.

notes.he: ר' יהושע בר' חנינא ויוחנן בן גודגדא לויים היו:
notes.en: Rabbi Yehoshua son of Rabbi Ḥanina and Yoḥanan ben Gudgeda were Levites. [So Rabbeinu Gershom’s text; the daf reads “bar Ḥananya.”]

messages.text: @Rabbi Yehoshua My son, go back, as you are among the singers and not among the gatekeepers.

What, is it not the case that these two Levite Sages disagree about this, that one Sage, Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Gudgeda, holds that if a Levite who is a singer closes the gate by himself, it is a prohibition punishable by death, and therefore the Sages decreed that a Levite who is a singer should not even assist the gatekeepers in closing the gates; and one Sage, Rabbi Yehoshua bar Ḥananya, holds that it is a prohibition that is not punishable by death, and therefore the Sages did not decree that a Levite who is a singer should not assist the gatekeepers in closing the gates?

notes.he: אם משוער לבדו וגזרו בו רבנן מסייע עם אחר ומ"ס באזהרה ולא גזרו רבנן אם בא לסייע:
notes.en: For one Sage holds it is [liable] to death: if he serves as a gatekeeper by himself, and the Rabbis decreed concerning one who assists another; and one Sage holds it is a prohibition, and the Rabbis did not decree if he comes to assist.

notes.he: יוחנן בן גודגדא דבמיתה הוו וגזרו רבנן דלא מסייע אטו שלא יהא שוער [לבדו] דבמיתה:
notes.en: For one Sage holds: Yoḥanan ben Gudgeda, that they are [liable] to death, and the Rabbis decreed that one should not assist, lest he serve as a gatekeeper [by himself], which is [liable] to death.

notes.he: ומר סבר ר' יהושע בן חנניה אינו אלא באזהרה הואיל ולית ביה עון מיתה וקא בעי לסיועיה דלא עביד ממש [לא גזרו רבנן]:
notes.en: And one Sage holds: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Ḥananya, that it is only a prohibition; since there is no sin of death in it, and he only wants to assist him and not actually do it, [the Rabbis did not decree].

messages.text: No, that is not necessarily the correct analysis of the baraita. Rather, everyone agrees that one Levite performing another Levite’s task by himself is a prohibition that is not punishable by death. One Sage holds that the Sages nevertheless decreed that a Levite who is a singer should not even assist the gatekeepers, and one Sage holds that the Sages did not decree that a Levite who is a singer should not assist the gatekeepers in closing the gates.

notes.he: לא דכולי עלמא כו':
notes.en: No, everyone [agrees] etc.

messages.text: Does a communal voluntary burnt offering require an accompanying song or does it not require song?

notes.he: כגון קיץ המזבח הבא מן השופרות שנותנין בהן מעות מותר חטאת ומותר אשם:
notes.en: A communal voluntary burnt offering: such as the “dessert of the altar” [kayitz hamizbe’aḥ], which comes from the horn-shaped collection boxes into which they put the money left over from sin offerings and the money left over from guilt offerings.

notes.he: כגון עולת קיץ אבל דיחיד אפי' חובתו אין טעונה נסכים:
notes.en: Does a communal voluntary burnt offering require song: such as the “dessert” burnt offering [of the altar]; but of an individual, even his obligatory offering does not require libations [so the printed text].

notes.he: שנעשה להן נס ונתנדבו להביא עולה (דעולת נדב' יחיד דתדיר' ודאי:
notes.en: A communal voluntary burnt offering: when a miracle was done for them and they volunteered to bring a burnt offering. (For an individual’s voluntary burnt offering, which is frequent, certainly

notes.he: אינה נ"ל) עולת נדבת יחיד דתדירא ודאי טעונה שירה [אינה טעונה נ"ל]:
notes.en: does not require [song], it seems to me.) An individual’s voluntary burnt offering, which is frequent, certainly requires song [corrected in brackets to: does not require song, it seems to me].

messages.text: The Merciful One states in the Torah: “You shall blow with the trumpets over your burnt offerings.” Does the term “burnt offerings” include both an obligatory burnt offering and a voluntary burnt offering, or perhaps the Merciful One is saying that the trumpets and song must accompany the burnt offerings of the entire Jewish people, i.e., they must be burnt offerings that are an obligation of the people?

verse.he: וּבְיוֹם שִׂמְחַתְכֶם וּבְמוֹעֲדֵיכֶם וּבְרָאשֵׁי חׇדְשֵׁיכֶם וּתְקַעְתֶּם בַּחֲצֹצְרֹת עַל עֹלֹתֵיכֶם וְעַל זִבְחֵי שַׁלְמֵיכֶם וְהָיוּ לָכֶם לְזִכָּרוֹן לִפְנֵי אֱלֹהֵיכֶם אֲנִי יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֵיכֶם׃ {פ}
verse.en: And on your joyous occasions—your fixed festivals and new moon days—you shall sound the trumpets over your burnt offerings and your sacrifices of well-being. They shall be a reminder of you before your God: I, the ETERNAL, am your God.

notes.he: ותקעתם בחצוצרות על עולותיכם (במדבר י׳:י׳) והיינו שירה:
notes.en: Your burnt offerings: “And you shall blow with the trumpets over your burnt offerings” (Numbers 10:10), and this is [the source for] song.

notes.he: או דלמא הא דקאמר ותקעתם [בחצוצרות] על עולותיכם דהיינו [שיר]:
notes.en: Or perhaps when it says “And you shall blow [with the trumpets] over your burnt offerings,” which is [song],

notes.he: עולותיכם דכולהו ישראל קאמר עולת נדבה בכל (ישראל) [יחיד] או עולת תמיד דהויא דכולהו ישראל:
notes.en: “your burnt offerings” speaks of all Israel.) [The editor notes:] It seems it should read: “your burnt offerings” speaks of all Israel, and that is the daily burnt offering, which belongs to all Israel; but a voluntary burnt offering is in the category of an individual’s burnt offering and does not require song. [The question is whether it means] a voluntary burnt offering of an (Israel) [individual], or the daily burnt offering, which belongs to all Israel.

messages.text: Come and hear a proof from a verse: “And Hezekiah commanded to offer the burnt offering upon the altar, and when the burnt offering began, the song of the Lord began also, and the trumpets, together with the instruments of David king of Israel…And Hezekiah the king and the princes commanded the Levites to sing praises unto the Lord.”
messages.quote: Does a communal voluntary burnt offering require an accompanying song

verse.he: וַיֹּאמֶר חִזְקִיָּהוּ לְהַעֲלוֹת הָעֹלָה לְהַמִּזְבֵּחַ וּבְעֵת הֵחֵל הָעוֹלָה הֵחֵל שִׁיר־יְהֹוָה וְהַחֲצֹצְרוֹת וְעַל־יְדֵי כְּלֵי דָּוִיד מֶלֶךְ־יִשְׂרָאֵל׃ וְכׇל־הַקָּהָל מִשְׁתַּחֲוִים וְהַשִּׁיר מְשׁוֹרֵר וְהַחֲצֹצְרוֹת (מחצצרים) [מַחְצְרִים] הַכֹּל עַד לִכְלוֹת הָעֹלָה׃ וּכְכַלּוֹת לְהַעֲלוֹת כָּרְעוּ הַמֶּלֶךְ וְכׇל־הַנִּמְצְאִים אִתּוֹ וַיִּשְׁתַּחֲווּ׃ וַיֹּאמֶר יְחִזְקִיָּהוּ הַמֶּלֶךְ וְהַשָּׂרִים לַלְוִיִּם לְהַלֵּל לַיהֹוָה בְּדִבְרֵי דָוִיד וְאָסָף הַחֹזֶה וַיְהַלְלוּ עַד־לְשִׂמְחָה וַיִּקְּדוּ וַיִּשְׁתַּחֲווּ׃ {פ}
verse.en: Hezekiah gave the order to offer the burnt offering on the altar. When the burnt offering began, the song of GOD and the trumpets began also, together with the instruments of King David of Israel. All the congregation prostrated themselves, the song was sung and the trumpets were blown—all this until the end of the burnt offering. When the offering was finished, the king and all who were there with him knelt and prostrated themselves. King Hezekiah and the officers ordered the Levites to praise GOD in the words of David and Asaph the seer; so they praised rapturously, and they bowed and prostrated themselves.

notes.he: משמע שהיה נמלך:
notes.en: And Hezekiah commanded [lit. said]: this implies that he was consulted.

notes.he: אע"ג דהאי קרא בפר עבודת כוכבים דב"ד (כו') [כתיב] הא איכא [נמי] מהתם שבעה כבשים דלאו הוו דע"ז אילימא דעולת חובה. דתמיד:
notes.en: And Hezekiah commanded [to offer the burnt offering, etc.]: even though this verse is written about the bull [brought by] the court for idol worship, there are also, there, seven lambs that were not for idol worship. If we say [it was] an obligatory burnt offering, of the daily offering,

messages.text: This song, what was its purpose? If we say that it accompanied an obligatory burnt offering that was brought on that day, why did they have to seek authorization from Hezekiah? Why did Hezekiah need to issue a specific command that they should accompany this offering with song? Rather, is it not the case that this song served to accompany the voluntary burnt offering that Hezekiah brought on that day?

notes.he: ונמלך אם ישוררו וכתיב החל שיר ה' שהורו לו ב"ד לשורר:
notes.en: Rather, is it not a voluntary offering: and he was consulted whether they should sing; and it is written “the song of the Lord began,” [meaning] that the court instructed him to have them sing.

notes.he: למה לי אימלוכי בחזקיהו (דאמר להו) [דקאמר] ויאמר חזקיה (אי לא) [והרי] ידעי דבעיא שיר:
notes.en: why did he need to consult Hezekiah, as it says “And Hezekiah commanded”? [Surely] they knew that it requires song.

messages.text: No, that day was a New Moon, and it was the additional burnt offering of the New Moon, an obligatory burnt offering, that was accompanied by the song. As for the need for Hezekiah’s approval, the explanation is as follows: It was the thirtieth day following the previous New Moon, and they were asking him if the current New Moon was established in its time, i.e., on that day, so that the burnt offering of the New Moon should be sacrificed, or if the New Moon had not been declared on that day. Hezekiah clarified that the court had declared the New Moon, and therefore they should sacrifice the offering.
messages.quote: why did they have to seek authorization from Hezekiah

notes.he: דמוסף הואי:
notes.en: The burnt offering of the New Moon: which was an additional offering.

messages.text: @Rav Yosef And how can you say that that day was the New Moon? Isn’t it written: “On the sixteenth day of the first month,” and later, in that context, it states: “And Hezekiah commanded to offer the burnt offering upon the altar”?
messages.quote: that day was a New Moon

verse.he: וַיָּחֵלּוּ בְּאֶחָד לַחֹדֶשׁ הָרִאשׁוֹן לְקַדֵּשׁ וּבְיוֹם שְׁמוֹנָה לַחֹדֶשׁ בָּאוּ לְאוּלָם יְהֹוָה וַיְקַדְּשׁוּ אֶת־בֵּית־יְהֹוָה לְיָמִים שְׁמוֹנָה וּבְיוֹם שִׁשָּׁה עָשָׂר לַחֹדֶשׁ הָרִאשׁוֹן כִּלּוּ׃ {ס}
verse.en: They began the sanctification on the first day of the first month; on the eighth day of the month they reached the porch of GOD. They sanctified the House of GOD for eight days, and on the sixteenth day of the first month they finished.

notes.he: ביום ט"ז [לחדש הראשון] אלמא לאו ר"ח הוא:
notes.en: On the sixteenth day [of the first month]: evidently it is not the New Moon.

messages.text: The question they were asking Hezekiah referred to the obligatory, communal burnt offering lamb that comes with the omer, i.e., the barley offering brought on the sixteenth of the first month, Nisan. They asked: Was the New Moon of Nisan established in its correct time, which means that it is now in fact the sixteenth of Nisan and the omer offering and the lamb brought with it should be sacrificed, or was it not really the sixteenth of Nisan?

notes.he: דהוא עולת חובה בי"ו בניסן:
notes.en: The lamb that comes with the omer: which is an obligatory burnt offering on the sixteenth of Nisan.

notes.dh: אלא אמר רמי בריה דרב ייבא כבש הבא עם העומר קא מיבעיא ליה
notes.he: טובא תימה מאי ס"ד דהא אתמול הקריבו תמידין ומוספין אמאי לא אימלך אלא ממוסף ט"ז דניסן:
notes.en: Rather, Rami son of Rav Yeiva said: they were asking about the lamb that comes with the omer: This is very puzzling. What was he thinking? For the day before they had offered the daily offerings and the additional offerings; why did they consult only about the additional offering of the sixteenth of Nisan?

notes.he: וקשה לרש"י דבדברי הימים כתיב האי קרא מקמי ויועץ המלך לעשות הפסח בחדש השני:
notes.en: They were asking whether the New Moon was established: And there is a difficulty for Rashi, for in Chronicles this verse is written before “And the king took counsel… to perform the Passover in the second month” (II Chronicles 30:2).

messages.text: How is it possible that they were unsure whether it was the sixteenth of Nisan? Let them see how the Paschal offering was performed on the fourteenth of Nisan and how matza was eaten the following night. The day of the sixteenth of Nisan could easily be determined from when those mitzvot were performed.
messages.quote: Was the New Moon of Nisan established in its correct time

notes.dh: כבש הבא עם העומר (זמנו בט"ז בניסן)
notes.he: [הוא דקרב בט"ז בניסן אי איקבע ר"ח בזמנו דיקרב עומר בט"ז] ולמה להו למיבעי וליחזו היכי עבוד פסח בי"ד והיכי אכול מצה דודאי לא הוו עבדי אי לאו דידעי דאיקבע בזמניה:
notes.en: The lamb that comes with the omer: [which is offered on the sixteenth of Nisan, if the New Moon was established in its time, so that the omer would be offered on the sixteenth]. And why did they need to ask? Let them see how they performed the Paschal offering on the fourteenth and how they ate matza, for certainly they would not have done so unless they knew that it had been established in its time.

messages.text: They asked permission from Hezekiah before sacrificing the lamb that comes with the omer offering, just as it is with regard to a prayer leader, who, as a gesture of respect, asks permission from the congregation before leading them in prayer. Likewise, the people asked permission from Hezekiah as a formal gesture of respect, not because they required his advice.

notes.he: הא דמימלך לאו משום דמספקא ליה דודאי הוקבע ר"ח בזמנו אלא רשותא הוא דקא נסיב:
notes.en: Rather, Rav Ashi said: this consulting was not because they were in doubt, for certainly the New Moon had been established in its time; rather, he was taking permission.

notes.he: ונסיב רשותא אם יתפלל:
notes.en: Just as with a prayer leader who consults: and takes permission whether he should pray.

notes.dh: אלא אמר רב (שימי) [אשי] מידי דהוי אשליח דציבורא דממליך
notes.he: ולעולם לא תפשוט דנימא דכבש הבא עם העומר הוה:
notes.en: Rather, Rav (Shimi) [Ashi] said: just as with a prayer leader who consults: and in truth you cannot resolve [the dilemma from here], for we may say that it was the lamb that comes with the omer.

notes.he: לעולם ידעי דאיקבע בזמניה וכבש הבא עם העומר הוה ודקא אמרת למה להו אימלוכי:
notes.en: Rather: in truth they knew that it had been established in its time, and it was the lamb that comes with the omer; and as for what you said, why did they need to consult [him]:

notes.he: [דמימלך] דנוטל רשות קודם [שיעמוד] להתפלל מפני כבוד הציבור אף הני נמי משום כבודו של מלך נטלו רשות ממנו ויש תימה בדבר היכי מצי אמר דאקרוב עומר בי"ו ניסן והרי עיבר חזקיהו ניסן בניסן כדמפורש [בדברי הימים]:
notes.en: Just as with a prayer leader [who consults], who takes permission before [he stands] to pray, out of respect for the congregation; so too these took permission from him out of respect for the king. And there is a puzzle in this: how can he say that they offered the omer on the sixteenth of Nisan, when Hezekiah intercalated Nisan in Nisan, as is explained [in Chronicles]?

messages.text: Now that you have arrived at this explanation, you may even say that it was a common obligatory burnt offering, e.g., the daily offering, and they asked permission of Hezekiah before sacrificing it, just as it is with regard to a prayer leader, who asks permission from the congregation before leading it in prayer.

notes.he: עולת תמיד שבכל יום ויום הואי:
notes.en: You may even say an obligatory burnt offering: it was the daily burnt offering of each and every day.

messages.text: The Gemara has still not proven whether or not a communal voluntary burnt offering must be accompanied with song. Come and hear a proof from the following baraita.
A fortunate matter is brought about on an auspicious day, and a deleterious matter on an inauspicious day.

notes.he: בניסן נגאלו בניסן עתידין להיגאל:
notes.en: Merit on an auspicious day: in Nisan they were redeemed, and in Nisan they will be redeemed in the future.

messages.text: As the Sages said: When the Temple was destroyed for the first time, that day was the Ninth of Av, a date on which several calamities had already occurred; and it was the conclusion of Shabbat, i.e., it was on the day after Shabbat, a Sunday; and it was the year after a Sabbatical Year; and it was the week of the priestly watch of Jehoiarib; and the priests and Levites were standing on their platform and singing song.

notes.he: אחד בשבת:
notes.en: The conclusion of Shabbat: Sunday [lit. the first day of the week].

notes.he: שמינית:
notes.en: And the conclusion of the Sabbatical Year: the eighth year.

notes.he: דהיינו יום חיב באותו יום שבכו העדה דכתיב ותשא כל העדה וגו':
notes.en: That day was the Ninth of Av: that is, an inauspicious day, the same day on which the congregation wept, as it is written: “And all the congregation lifted up [their voice]” (Numbers 14:1).

messages.text: And what song were they singing? They were singing the verse: “And He brought upon them their own iniquity, and He will cut them off in their own evil.” And they did not manage to recite the end of that verse: “The Lord our God will cut them off,” before gentiles came and conquered them. And likewise, the same happened when the Second Temple was destroyed.

verse.he: וַיָּשֶׁב עֲלֵיהֶם ׀ אֶת־אוֹנָם וּבְרָעָתָם יַצְמִיתֵם יַצְמִיתֵם יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֵינוּ׃ {פ}
verse.en:
Their evil will be made to recoil upon them,
through their own wickedness they will be annihilated;
the ETERNAL our God will annihilate them.

notes.he: פסוק הוא בתהלים במזמור אל נקמות ה':
notes.en: And He brought upon them their own iniquity: it is a verse in Psalms, in the psalm “God of vengeance, Lord” (Psalms 94).

notes.he: כשחרב הבית בשניה מוצאי שבת ומוצאי שביעית היתה:
notes.en: And likewise in the second: when the Temple was destroyed the second time, it was the conclusion of Shabbat and the conclusion of the Sabbatical Year.

messages.text: This song, what was its purpose? If we say that it accompanied an obligatory burnt offering, was there any obligatory communal burnt offering sacrificed at that time? The daily offering had already ceased to be sacrificed, due to a lack of animals, on the seventeenth of Tammuz, three weeks before the Ninth of Av. Rather, is it not correct to say that this song accompanied a voluntary burnt offering?
messages.quote: And what song were they singing?

notes.he: שלא היו להם כבשים מחמת שהיו צרים על ירושלים ואין יוצא ובא:
notes.en: The daily offering ceased: for they had no lambs, because [the enemy] were besieging Jerusalem and no one could go out or come in.

notes.he: שלא היה להם [שוב] בהמה להקריב:
notes.en: The daily offering ceased: for they had no more animals to offer.

messages.text: And can you understand this to be the case? What is different about an obligatory burnt offering, which was not sacrificed at this time because they did not have animals to bring, and what is different about a voluntary burnt offering, that it was sacrificed? Just as there were no animals available for obligatory offerings, there were none available for voluntary burnt offerings either.

notes.he: הלא לא היו כבשים מצויים:
notes.en: And what is different about a voluntary burnt offering, that it was [sacrificed]: weren’t lambs unavailable?

messages.text: That is not difficult. A young bull, which cannot be sacrificed as the daily offering, for which lambs are required, happened to come into their possession merely by coincidence, and they sacrificed it as a voluntary burnt offering. This indicates that the Levites are required to sing as an accompaniment to the sacrifice of a communal voluntary burnt offering.

notes.dh: הא לא קשיא בן בקר בעלמא אתרמי להו
notes.he: שאינו ראוי לתמיד וראוי לעולת נדבה:
notes.en: That is not difficult; a young bull merely happened to come to them: which is not fit for the daily offering but is fit for a voluntary burnt offering.

notes.he: שמצאו בהמה והקריבוה עולת נדבה:
notes.en: [That happened to come to them: that they found an animal and offered it as a voluntary burnt offering.

messages.text: And how can you understand the description of the destruction cited in the baraita? The song of the day for Sunday, which is when the baraita says that the Temple was destroyed, is the psalm that begins: “The earth is the Lord’s, and the fullness thereof.” And yet the verse that the baraita says that the Levites were singing, “And He brought upon them their own iniquity,” is in the song for Wednesday, not the song for Sunday.
messages.quote: And He brought upon them their own iniquity

verse.he: לְדָוִד מִזְמוֹר לַיהֹוָה הָאָרֶץ וּמְלוֹאָהּ תֵּבֵל וְיֹשְׁבֵי בָהּ׃
verse.en:
Of David. A psalm.
The earth is GOD’s and all that it holds,
the world and its inhabitants.

notes.he: דשירה גמורה הויא ההיא שירה על קרבן והא שירה דאחד בשבת לה' הארץ ומלואה כדאמר בראש השנה (דף לא.) והאי קרא במזמור אל נקמות ה' שהוא שיר של רביעי בשבת:
notes.en: And can you understand: that that song was a full song over an offering? But the song of Sunday is “The earth is the Lord’s, and the fullness thereof,” as it says in Rosh HaShana (31a), and this verse is in the psalm “God of vengeance, Lord,” which is the song of Wednesday [lit. the fourth day of the week].

notes.dh: שירה דיומא לה' הארץ ומלואה (תהילים כ״ד:א׳)
notes.he: ואם עולת קיץ טעונה שירה היינו שיר שאמרו בתמיד של שחר בו ביום:
notes.en: The song of the day is “The earth is the Lord’s, and the fullness thereof” (Psalms 24:1): and if the “dessert” burnt offering requires song, it would be the song that they said with the morning daily offering on that day.

notes.he: דשירה דוקא הואי. הא שירה דיומיה דנאמר ביו' ראשון דהיינו מוצאי שבת לה' הארץ ומלואה הוא. וישב עליהם את אונם שירה דארבע בשבא הוא דכת' בסוף מזמור אל נקמות דנאמר ברביעי אלא לאו משום שיר ממש אמרו ליה:
notes.en: And can you understand: that it was specifically song [over an offering]? But the song of the day said on the first day, that is, at the conclusion of Shabbat, is “The earth is the Lord’s, and the fullness thereof”; “And He brought upon them their own iniquity” is the song of Wednesday, for it is written at the end of the psalm “God of vengeance,” which is said on the fourth day. Rather, they did not say it as an actual song.

messages.text: Rather, it was merely a portentous lamentation [eiliyya] that came into their mouths, not an actual song recited over an offering.

notes.he: קינה כדמתרגמינן ושאי על שפים קינה וטלי על נגדין אילייא (ירמיהו ז׳:כ״ט):
notes.en: Eiliyya: a lamentation, as the Targum renders “and take up a lamentation on the high hills” (Jeremiah 7:29) with the word eiliyya.

notes.he: קינה נזדמנה בפיהם:
notes.en: Rather, merely a lamentation: a lament that happened to come into their mouths.

messages.text: But isn’t it taught in the baraita that the Levites were standing on their platform near the altar, which is where they stood when they sang to accompany offerings?

notes.he: דוכן כמין אצטבא היה:
notes.en: The platform [dukhan] was a kind of bench.

notes.he: והא עומדין על דוכנן קתני דמשמע שהלכו שם לשום כך לומר שירה ובשביל עולת נדבה (לא הוי כולם עולין לשם) [לא הויא כולם עולין לשם עולה]:
notes.en: But it teaches “standing on their platform,” which implies that they went there for this purpose, to say song; and for a voluntary burnt offering they would not all go up there.

messages.text: The Levites are permitted to recite songs on the platform even when it is not for an offering.
messages.lead: This can be explained in accordance with the opinion of Reish Lakish, who says:

notes.dh: אלא סבירא ליה כריש לקיש דאומר שירה שלא על הקרבן
notes.he: אע"ג דאין מחוייבין כשאין תמידין:
notes.en: Rather, he holds like Reish Lakish, who says one recites song not over an offering, even though they are not obligated when there are no daily offerings.

messages.text: If so, if the Levites may recite songs on the platform at will, let them also recite a song for a voluntary burnt offering, even if it is not required.

notes.he: דאפילו שלא על הקרבן אומר שירה בעולת נדבה נמי לימא ותפשוט בעיא דר' אבין:
notes.en: If so: that one recites song even when it is not over an offering, let him also recite it for a voluntary burnt offering, and you would resolve Rabbi Avin’s dilemma.

notes.he: פי' בקונטרס ותפשוט בעיא דרבי אבין:
notes.en: If so, for a voluntary burnt offering: the Kuntres [Rashi] explains: and you would resolve Rabbi Avin’s dilemma.

notes.he: (בעולה נמי נדבת) [בעולת יחיד] נמי נימא אע"ג דאין מחוייבין:
notes.en: (For a voluntary burnt offering also) [For an individual’s burnt offering] also let them say it, even though they are not obligated.

messages.text: That could result in a mishap, as the Levites might assume that just as singing for a voluntary burnt offering is optional, so too singing for an obligatory burnt offering is also optional.

notes.he: דהא דר"ל רשות הוא דאי אית ליה לעולת נדבה ברשות אתי למימר עולת חובה נמי רשות הלכך לא אמרינן שיר לגמרי בנדבה:
notes.en: It would result in a mishap: for this [song] of Reish Lakish is optional, and if one sang for a voluntary burnt offering as an option, people would come to say that [song for] an obligatory burnt offering is also optional. Therefore we do not recite song at all for a voluntary offering.

notes.he: דאמרי ש"מ עולת נדבה לא מצי קרבה בלא שיר [וזמנין דליכא לוים כמו שעלה עזרא וסברי דלא מצי קרבה בלא שיר] ולא מייתו לה ואיהי לא בעיא שיר:
notes.en: It would result in a mishap: for they would say: Learn from this that a voluntary burnt offering cannot be offered without song; [and sometimes there are no Levites, as when Ezra went up, and they would think that it cannot be offered without song,] and they would not bring it, though it does not require song.

notes.he: ואיכא דאמרי נפיק מינה חורבה דאמרי מה עולת נדבה איבעי אמר איבעי לא אמר [אף האי עולת חובה איבעי אמר ואיבעי לא אמר. למ"ה]:
notes.en: And some say: it would result in a mishap, for they would say: just as with a voluntary burnt offering one may say [song] if he wishes and not say it if he wishes, so too with this obligatory burnt offering, one may say it if he wishes and not say it if he wishes.

messages.text: The question of whether a song must be recited for a communal voluntary burnt offering has still not been resolved. What came of it, i.e., what is the resolution to that question? Come and hear a proof,
messages.quote: Does a communal voluntary burnt offering require an accompanying song or does it not require song?

notes.he: דבעיא דר' אבין:
notes.en: What came of it: of Rabbi Avin’s dilemma.

messages.text: “You shall blow with the trumpets over your burnt offerings, and over the sacrifices of your peace offerings,” juxtaposes burnt offerings to peace offerings, which indicates that there is a relevant comparison between them with regard to the sounding of trumpets, and, by extension, to song.
messages.lead: as Rav Mari, son of Rav Kahana, teaches that the verse:

verse.he: וּבְיוֹם שִׂמְחַתְכֶם וּבְמוֹעֲדֵיכֶם וּבְרָאשֵׁי חׇדְשֵׁיכֶם וּתְקַעְתֶּם בַּחֲצֹצְרֹת עַל עֹלֹתֵיכֶם וְעַל זִבְחֵי שַׁלְמֵיכֶם וְהָיוּ לָכֶם לְזִכָּרוֹן לִפְנֵי אֱלֹהֵיכֶם אֲנִי יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֵיכֶם׃ {פ}
verse.en: And on your joyous occasions—your fixed festivals and new moon days—you shall sound the trumpets over your burnt offerings and your sacrifices of well-being. They shall be a reminder of you before your God: I, the ETERNAL, am your God.

notes.dh: ותקעתם בחצוצרות על עולותיכם ועל זבחי שלמיכם
notes.he: מקיש עולה לשלמים ושלמים לעולה לענין שיר:
notes.en: And you shall blow with the trumpets over your burnt offerings and over the sacrifices of your peace offerings: it juxtaposes the burnt offering to peace offerings, and peace offerings to the burnt offering, with regard to song.

notes.he: לעולותיכם ולזבחי שלמיכם מה עולה קדשי קדשים אף שלמים כו' ומה שלמים שקבוע להן זמן וכו' - והא ברייתא איתא נמי בזבחים בפ' איזהו מקומן (זבחים דף נה.) ומתניא הכי מה עולה קדשי קדשים אף שלמים קדשי קדשים מה עולה טעונה צפון אף שלמים כו' וליכא התם ומה שלמים שקבוע להם זמן וכו' כדאיתא הכא ושמא כל זה דטעונין צפון ודקבוע להם זמן היא ברייתא וכן היה שונה אותה רב מרי הכי והתם תניא מה שהיה צריך ממנה א"נ אין בברייתא כי אם עולה קדשי קדשים אף שלמים קדשי קדשים (ה"נ ומקשינן) לענין קביעות זמן ולענין טעונה צפון דזבחים. רבינו אלחנן:
notes.en: “Your burnt offerings and the sacrifices of your peace offerings”: just as the burnt offering is of the most sacred order, so too peace offerings, etc.; and just as peace offerings have a set time, etc.: This baraita is found also in Zevaḥim, in chapter Eizehu Mekoman (Zevaḥim 55a), and it is taught there thus: Just as the burnt offering is of the most sacred order, so too peace offerings are of the most sacred order; just as the burnt offering requires [slaughter in] the north, so too peace offerings, etc. And it does not have there “and just as peace offerings have a set time, etc.,” as it is here. Perhaps all of it — that they require the north and that they have a set time — is one baraita, and Rav Mari taught it thus [here], while there [the Gemara] taught only what it needed of it. Alternatively, the baraita contains only “the burnt offering is of the most sacred order, so too peace offerings are of the most sacred order,” and [the Gemara] draws the further comparisons, with regard to a set time [here] and with regard to requiring the north in Zevaḥim. [So] Rabbeinu Elḥanan.

notes.he: ת"ש ותקעתם בחצוצרות על עולותיכם ועל זבחי שלמיכם מה עולה [דקדשי קדשים בעיא שיר חצוצרות אף שלמים קדשי קדשים היינו ב' כבשי עצרת דהוו שלמים ואין נאכלין אלא לכהן דומיא דחטאת ואשם דקדשים קדשי הן דכתיב קודש יהיו לה' לכהן] שקבוע להן זמן. בעצרת:
notes.en: Come and hear: “And you shall blow with the trumpets over your burnt offerings and over the sacrifices of your peace offerings”: just as the burnt offering [which is of the most sacred order requires song and trumpets, so too peace offerings of the most sacred order, that is, the two lambs of Atzeret, which are peace offerings and are eaten only by a priest, like the sin offering and the guilt offering, which are of the most sacred order, as it is written: “They shall be holy to the Lord for the priest”] have a set time: on Atzeret.

messages.text: There are two conclusions that are to be drawn from this comparison: Just as the burnt offering is an offering of the most sacred order, so too, the peace offering that must be accompanied by song is one that is an offering of the most sacred order, and the only peace offering of this kind is the lambs that are brought together with the two loaves on Shavuot.

notes.dh: מה עולה האמורה כאן קדשי קדשים
notes.he: דאין לך עולה קדשים קלים אף שלמים האמורים כאן טעונים שיר בשלמים קדשי קדשים משתעי ואין לך שלמים קדשי קדשים אלא כבשי עצרת דשלמי ציבור הן וכתיב בהו (ויקרא כ״ג:כ׳) קדש יהיו לה' לכהן ומה שלמים האמורים כאן לגבי שיר קבוע להן זמן דהא אוקימנא בכבשי עצרת אף עולה האמורה כאן שקבוע לה זמן לאפוקי נדבת ציבור דאין קבוע לה זמן:
notes.en: Just as the burnt offering stated here is of the most sacred order — for you have no burnt offering of lesser sanctity — so too the peace offerings stated here as requiring song: [the verse] speaks of peace offerings of the most sacred order, and you have no peace offerings of the most sacred order except the lambs of Atzeret [Shavuot], which are communal peace offerings, and of them it is written: “They shall be holy to the Lord for the priest” (Leviticus 23:20). And just as the peace offerings stated here with regard to song have a set time, since we have established them as the lambs of Atzeret, so too the burnt offering stated here is one that has a set time, to exclude a communal voluntary offering, which has no set time.

messages.text: And just as this peace offering has a set time when it must be brought, so too, the burnt offering that must be accompanied by song is one that has a set time, which excludes voluntary burnt offerings. Consequently, voluntary burnt offerings are not accompanied by song.

notes.he: היינו כל עולות חובות וקא ממעט מהכא עולה נדבה:
notes.en: So too a burnt offering that has a set time: that is, all obligatory burnt offerings; and from here [the verse] excludes a voluntary burnt offering.

messages.text: The discussion of the Levites’ song continues on 12a with a new dilemma: do libations brought by themselves, without an animal offering, require song?
